name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 district partisan lean in heavily Republican western Nebraska
Incumbent Adrian Smith seeking another term with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger Becky Stille has raised only about $55,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Smith's win probability near 96%
model.rationale: The R+27 lean, Smith's incumbency and roughly 30-to-1 fundraising advantage over Stille, and no outside spending against him all point to a comfortable Republican hold; markets agree at about 96% for Smith.
model.watch: A major shift in the national environment or unexpected late spending against Smith could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adrian Smith, the longtime Republican incumbent in this sprawling western Nebraska district, is seeking another term against Democrat Becky Stille. The district's R+27 partisan lean makes it one of the most Republican seats in the country, and Smith has never faced a close general election. He has built a substantial financial advantage, raising about $1.8 million and holding over $1 million on hand, while Stille has raised roughly $55,000 with little cash remaining.

No independent or outside groups are spending against Smith, and no public polling of the race exists. Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. An independent and another non-major candidate are also on the ballot but lack resources. All available evidence points to a safe Republican hold, with the only real question being the size of Smith's victory margin.
